extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example open-source dataset for training reasoning models via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). It covers math (850K), code (250K), and science (100K) domains. The dataset is constructed through a systematic pipeline involving question sourcing from 27 code, 21 math, and 14 science sources, question mixing, LLM-based question filtering, deduplication, multiple answer sampling (16x per question), and teacher model annotation using QwQ-32B. The dataset was developed through 1,000+ controlled experiments to identify the best data generation strategies. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on this dataset yields OpenThinker3-7B, a state-of-the-art open-data reasoning model at the 7B scale.
extraction.license: Multiple licenses apply to source datasets; see Appendix Q of the paper for details.
extraction.creator: OpenThoughts Team (Stanford University, University of Washington, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, JSC, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill, ASU, Lila Sciences, Cornell Tech, TUM, Open-Sci Collective)
extraction.citeAs: Guha, E., Marten, R., Keh, S., Raoof, N., Smymis, G., et al. (2025). Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through a multi-stage pipeline: (1) sourcing questions from 27 code, 21 math, and 14 science question sources including fully synthetic (LLM-generated), semi-synthetic (LLM using existing data as seeds), and non-synthetic (human-written) sources; (2) mixing top-performing question sources; (3) filtering questions using LLM-based difficulty or response length methods; (4) deduplicating questions and sampling 16 answers per question from a teacher model (QwQ-32B); and (5) no answer filtering was applied as it did not improve performance. The pipeline was developed through 1,000+ controlled ablation experiments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Experiments, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from existing datasets and newly generated datasets across math, code, and science domains. Math sources include OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath-1.5, MathPile, AutoMathText, DeepMath-103K, and others. Code sources include StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, KodCode-V1, and others. Science sources include StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs (SCP-116K and textbooks), CQADupStack-Physics, and others. Answers (reasoning traces) were generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were mixed from top-performing sources (top 1-2 sources per domain). For math and science, exact deduplication was applied using Normalized Indel similarity (LCS-based). For code, no deduplication was applied. 16 answers were sampled per question from QwQ-32B. No answer filtering was applied. Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks was performed using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13) methods.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Question filtering used LLM-based methods: difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code (rating 1-10 on ICPC rubric), and response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science. Deduplication used exact match for math and science. Decontamination removed training samples with high similarity to evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and 13-gram overlap. For science questions from PDFs, Gemini was used for OCR, GPT-4o-mini for question extraction and refinement, and additional filtering for relevance to organic chemistry and answerability.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers (reasoning traces) were generated by prompting the QwQ-32B teacher model to produce long chain-of-thought responses for each question. 16 answers were sampled per question. No answer filtering was applied in the final pipeline. For question filtering, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini were used to assess difficulty or generate responses for length-based selection. For question generation from unstructured text, GPT-4o-mini was used with specific prompts to extract or generate questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: QwQ-32B (teacher model for answer generation); GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini (for question filtering and question generation); DeepSeek API (used during pipeline experiments at ~$300 per 31,600-sample dataset); Gemini (gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 for PDF OCR)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No answer filtering strategy was found to outperform the baseline of using all generated answers. Verification methods (majority consensus, GPT verification, FastText filtering) did not significantly improve downstream model performance. For question filtering, LLM-based methods (difficulty-based and response length) outperformed classical methods (fastText, embedding-based). Decontamination achieved a 99.6% true negative rate on a manually constructed test set of 3,092 contaminated samples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (primary teacher model for answer generation), DeepSeek-R1 (used in earlier pipeline experiments), GPT-4o-mini (question filtering, difficulty scoring, question generation, verification), GPT-4.1-mini (response length filtering for math and science), GPT-4.1-nano (response length filtering), Gemini gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (PDF OCR), FastText classifiers (question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding-based filtering), Evalchemy (evaluation framework)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset released on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M. Codebase released at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts. The OpenThoughts project has gone through multiple generations (BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, OpenThoughts3-1.2M), suggesting ongoing development. No explicit deprecation policy stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables open-source development of strong reasoning models, democratizing access to training data for reasoning AI. However, safety analysis shows that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of base models. OpenThinker3-7B achieved a harmfulness rate of 55.5% on Harmbench (compared to 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), indicating a trade-off between reasoning capability and safety. The dataset was trained without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses exclusively on math, code, and science domains and does not cover other reasoning domains. Question sources are predominantly from competitive programming, mathematics competitions, and science olympiad problems, which may bias toward a particular style of reasoning. The dataset does not include reinforcement learning data. Safety analysis reveals that models trained on this data exhibit increased harmful response rates.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not cover reinforcement learning training regimes. It does not explore staged SFT or curriculum learning. The pipeline selects strategies that maximize overall average benchmark performance rather than optimizing per domain, which may limit domain-specific performance. The dataset is limited to math, code, and science domains. Models trained on this data show degraded safety alignment. The interaction between question diversity and answer diversity across different domains, dataset sizes, and model scales remains an open question.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science domains. The dataset is designed for training reasoning models that produce long chain-of-thought responses. It can also be used for studying data scaling laws for reasoning, investigating data curation strategies, and benchmarking reasoning dataset quality.
